label: Problem set 16
title: Problem set 16: Scanning probe techniques
summary: Practice with scanning probe electrochemistry: SECM feedback modes, approach curves, STM tunnelling and the combination of imaging with electrochemical control.

intro.text: Scanning probe techniques raster a small tip over a surface. SECM reads a current that depends on the tip-substrate distance and reactivity (feedback mode), while STM and AFM map topography by tunnelling current or force.
In SECM, a regenerating substrate raises the tip current (positive feedback) and an insulating one lowers it (negative feedback); approach curves record this.

sections.title: Hint sheet: scanning probe ideas
sections.summary: Practice with scanning probe electrochemistry: SECM feedback modes, approach curves, STM tunnelling and the combination of imaging with electrochemical control.
keyPoints: SECM tip current depends on tip-substrate distance
Positive feedback: conductive substrate raises tip current
Negative feedback: insulating substrate lowers it

blocks.text: Scanning probe techniques raster a small tip over a surface. SECM reads a current that depends on the tip-substrate distance and reactivity (feedback mode), while STM and AFM map topography by tunnelling current or force.
In SECM, a regenerating substrate raises the tip current (positive feedback) and an insulating one lowers it (negative feedback); approach curves record this.

questions.question: Scanning electrochemical microscopy (SECM) uses as its probe:
options: An ultramicroelectrode tip moved close to a substrate
A beam of electrons in vacuum
questions.explanation: SECM scans a small electrode tip near a surface and reads the current, which depends on the tip-substrate distance and the substrate reactivity.

questions.question: In the feedback mode of SECM, a conductive substrate regenerates the mediator and increases the tip current.
questions.explanation: When the substrate regenerates the mediator, its return to the tip adds to the measured current, so the tip current rises above its bulk value - positive feedback.

questions.question: In SECM feedback mode, an insulating substrate that blocks the mediator causes the tip current to:
options: Stay exactly at the bulk value
questions.explanation: An inert surface shields the tip and blocks diffusion of the mediator back to it, so the tip current falls - negative feedback.

questions.question: Scanning tunnelling microscopy (STM) measures a tunnelling current that falls sharply as the tip is lifted away from the surface.
questions.explanation: The tunnelling current decays roughly exponentially with distance, which is why STM can follow atomic-scale height changes so sensitively.

questions.question: Which techniques are scanning probe methods used in electrochemistry? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: SECM, STM and AFM all raster a probe over a surface to map it, and each can be combined with electrochemical control. X-ray crystallography is not a scanning probe method.

questions.question: An approach curve in SECM records the tip current as the tip is moved toward the substrate.
questions.explanation: The shape of the approach curve - rising (positive feedback) or falling (negative feedback) - identifies whether the substrate regenerates or blocks the mediator.

questions.question: In a positive-feedback SECM measurement the tip current close to the substrate is 1.5 times the bulk tip current. By what fraction is the current enhanced over the bulk value?
questions.explanation: Enhancement = 1.5 - 1.0 = 0.5, i.e. the current is 50 percent larger than in the bulk.

questions.question: Scanning tunnelling microscopy images a surface by:
options: Measuring a tunnelling current between a sharp tip and the surface
questions.explanation: A bias applied between a nanometre-sharp tip and a conducting surface produces a tunnelling current that depends steeply on the gap, so scanning the tip maps the surface.

questions.question: Atomic force microscopy maps a surface by measuring the force between a sharp probe and the sample.
questions.explanation: AFM feels the surface rather than tunnelling through it, so it works on insulators as well as conductors.

questions.question: In SECM feedback mode the tip current at a large tip-substrate distance equals the bulk value i_bulk. If close to a conductive substrate the current rises to 2.0 i_bulk, by what factor is the current enhanced?
questions.explanation: The normalized tip current near the substrate is 2.0 times the bulk value, so the enhancement factor is 2.0 (positive feedback).

questions.question: A key requirement of the SECM tip electrode is that it be:
options: Very small (an ultramicroelectrode) to localise the measurement
Very large to collect more current
questions.explanation: A tiny tip is needed so the measured current reflects a small, well-defined region and so the tip can approach close to the substrate.

questions.question: SECM can map the local reactivity of a surface, not just its topography.
questions.explanation: Because the tip current depends on how the substrate consumes or regenerates the mediator, SECM distinguishes chemically active regions, a functional map rather than a purely topographic one.
